newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore opposition politician faces joint suit.
newsitem.headline: Singapore opposition politician faces joint suit.

text.p: Singapore Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew and his son, Deputy Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong, have filed a joint defamation suit against opposition politician Tang Liang Hong, a legal notice published on Monday said.

As of late last week Tang already faced at least nine suits for defamation brought by various members of Singapore's ruling People's Action Party (PAP) since the country's general election on January 2, in which the PAP won 81 of 83 parliamentary seats.

Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong and 10 other leading PAP members, including the Lees, are also suing Workers' Party (WP) leader Joshua Jeyaretnam for defamation over comments he is said to have made at a WP rally on January 1.
The Monday notice of the Lees' action against Tang alleges they were slandered by him in comments on three occasions during the election campaign, in which he stood as a WP candidate.
The notice, published in the daily Straits Times newspaper, gave no details of the exact remarks at issue.
Lawyers for the Lees and Tang were not immediately available for comment on the notice.
Tang faces an injunction seeking to freeze his assets or have him set aside up to S$11.2 million (US$7.94 million) for possible damages and legal costs in relation to the earlier lawsuits.
The injunction was filed on behalf of 11 members of the PAP, including the prime minister.
Tang is in London consulting lawyers on his defence strategy. He left Singapore shortly after the election campaign, saying he had received death threats.

Tang and Jeyaretnam lost their bids in a hotly contested multi-member constituency in the January poll. But Jeyaretnam will still get a seat in parliament under a constitutional provision for a seat for best-loser if only two opposition members are elected.
Tang's wife, Teo Siew Har, was cited as a co-defendant in the Lees' writ.
Spouses are sometimes cited as co-defendants in such suits if a court suspects some of a principal defendant's assets may be in their partner's name, a Singapore lawyer has told Reuters.
The PAP leaders filed the original defamation suits against Tang for calling them "liars" during the election campaign.

During the campaign Goh had called Tang a "Chinese chauvinist" dangerous to Singapore's racial harmony. Tang denied the charges and filed police reports saying the allegations were groundless and intended to harm his reputation. ($1 = S$1.41)
